data.topic: Simplify memory infrastructure: reduce persistence surfaces, make Stop hook async, fix schema migration bug, purge OpenMemory bloat, dedupe embedding code
data.input_summary: Fix the broken behavioral learning pipeline (schema migration bug), reduce 7 persistence surfaces to 3, make Stop hook async via background subprocess, purge 49% bloat from OpenMemory, and extract shared embedding utilities.

decisions.choice: Accept the dependency. Add a warning in the Stop hook when Ollama is unavailable so degradation is visible, not silent. Do not add regex or simhash fallback for correction detection.
decisions.reasoning: decision-74 deliberately chose semantic embeddings. The Ollama dependency is the cost of high-quality correction detection. Making it visible (warning) is sufficient — users can start Ollama if they want learning active.

decisions.choice: Keep current embedding-based dedup. Fix the real problems: purge 366 legacy/orphaned entries from OpenMemory, stop re-embedding 3 static tool-learnings entries every session end.
decisions.reasoning: Tiered dedup is an optimization that doesn't address the actual bottleneck (unnecessary work on bloated data). Clean the DB first, then reassess if dedup performance is still a concern.

decisions.choice: Kill 4 surfaces: correction-tallies.jsonl (dead, replaced by correction_groups), om-ops.json (write-only, zero readers — replace with stderr), tool-learnings.md (move entirely to OpenMemory), corrections.md (move entries into correction_groups DB directly). Reduces 7 surfaces to 3: correction_groups in epics.db, rendered-prefs.md sidecar, openmemory.sqlite.
decisions.reasoning: Aggressive consolidation. corrections.md is already parsed by signal_processor.py — making the DB the sole source eliminates the dual-write. tool-learnings.md duplicates what's in OpenMemory. The other two are dead/debug-only.

decisions.choice: Background subprocess via nohup/disown. Stop hook keeps fast sections (mtime comparison, <1s) synchronous. Heavy sections (signal processing, session summary, tool learning sync, auto-distillation) spawned as background Python process. Main hook exits immediately.
decisions.reasoning: Reduces exit latency from ~2-5s to <1s. Background process writes to DB; next session start reads. No race condition — different sessions, different processes.

decisions.choice: Fix correction_groups table to add text and source columns. Run migration on existing data. This unblocks the entire behavioral learning pipeline — rendered-prefs.md has been blank.
decisions.reasoning: Scout found the text column doesn't exist despite being referenced by the renderer. 4 promoted entries exist but their text can't be accessed. This is the highest priority item — everything else is optimization on a broken system.

decisions.choice: Extract _get_embedding, _cosine_similarity, _embedding_to_blob, _blob_to_embedding into a shared module (~/.claude/hooks/lib/embedding_utils.py). Both signal_processor.py and om_write.py import from it.
decisions.reasoning: ~80 lines duplicated across two files. Single source of truth for embedding operations, Ollama URL config, similarity thresholds.

decisions.choice: One-time purge of 366 legacy/orphaned entries (261 transcript entries + 105 entries with tags outside ALLOWED_TAGS). Reduces DB from 749 to ~383 entries.
decisions.reasoning: 49% of the DB is bloat from before tag enforcement was added. Dedup and budget enforcement are doing unnecessary work against entries that should never have been stored.

constraints.value: decision-74 (ACTIVE): semantic embeddings for correction detection. No regex fallback.
decision-73 (ACTIVE): rendered-prefs.md sidecar via @import must remain compaction-resilient.
decision-75 (ACTIVE): single authority for correction pipeline in signal_processor.py.
epics.db ownership: Gemini writes via pm_* tools, Claude writes only plan_file and state.
